title: Weekly Homework Tear-Off Pad
whatYouGet: A weekly tear-off homework pad with daily microtasks, parent-visible instructions and a teacher key.
howToUse: Set the week's objectives and workload, approve the daily progression, then print and bind the pad.
effectiveUsage: 1. Define the five daily objectives and time cap.
2. Paste approved tasks or allow clearly labelled original practice.
3. Review answer and workload parity across days.
4. Compile through a free Overleaf login, print a week and test the tear line.
commonFix: If wrong, reply with: "Rebalance the daily time, keep each tear-off self-contained and move every answer to the teacher-only key."
promptText:
ROLE: Act as a weekly homework planner and tear-off pad typesetter.

CONTEXT: A [CLASS] class needs five short home-practice slips for [WEEKLY TOPIC] with a fixed daily time cap.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:
- [CLASS]
- [WEEKLY TOPIC]
- [DAILY OBJECTIVES]
- [APPROVED TASKS OR ORIGINAL-PRACTICE PERMISSION]
- [DAILY TIME CAP]
- [PARENT NOTE]

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:
- [OVERLEAF] Whitelist: https://www.overleaf.com/docs?encoded_snip={PERCENT_ENCODED_LATEX}. Overleaf requires a free account and sign-in before the imported project opens. Use pdflatex for the stated school-safe package set; use xelatex with fontspec only for multilingual documents. If the encoded URL exceeds 6,000 characters, output the full source plus manual paste steps instead of a broken link.
- [WOLFRAMALPHA] Whitelist: https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i={ENCODED_PLAIN_CALCULATOR_QUERY}. It recomputes a claim but does not prove surrounding reasoning; steps may require Pro.
- [KHAN_ACADEMY] Whitelist: https://www.khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query={ENCODED_KEYWORDS}. Use search only; never invent opaque Khan topic or exercise paths.

DO THIS:
1. Map one attainable objective and retrieval item to each day.
2. Estimate solution time and flag any day that exceeds the cap.
3. Make each slip self-contained with date, task, workspace and a brief parent-facing instruction.
4. Place answers and likely misconceptions in a teacher-only weekly key.
5. Add crop or perforation guides and binding instructions that preserve all text.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
Example task: Add a Friday self-check for solving 2x+5=17.
Expected result or check target: The teacher key records x=6 and the student slip receives only a check-this-yourself route after the attempt.
check this yourself
CHECK → https://www.wolframalpha.com/input?i=solve%202x%2B5%3D17
(paste-fallback: solve 2x+5=17)
Encoding note: The space, plus sign and equals sign are encoded so the decoded query is exactly the fallback.

OUTPUT FORMAT:
1. Weekly Map — objective, task type and time by day
2. Tear-Off Slips — five self-contained student sections
3. Teacher Key — answers and misconception notes
4. Production Guide — print, trim, perforate and bind steps

QUALITY AND TOOL GUARDRAILS:
- Do not promise that estimated time fits every learner; label it as a planning estimate.
- Overleaf requires a free account and login wherever its route is used.
- Use pdflatex for English-only slips and xelatex only for multilingual scripts.
- Typst is paste-only and non-LaTeX; no content-prefill URL exists.
- Label newly authored questions ORIGINAL PRACTICE, never PYQ or official board material.
- Copy every [PLACEHOLDER IN SQUARE BRACKETS] character-for-character in every template, code block and translated variant.
- Never output a desmos.com URL with parameters, a mathsolver.microsoft.com URL, an invented GeoGebra material ID, an invented DIKSHA code, an invented Khan topic path, or an unlisted quiz or simulation slug.
- Never describe an AI answer as verified. Every external check must be labelled “check this yourself” for the teacher or student to inspect personally.
- Do not invent exam facts, source citations, marks distributions, tool IDs or inaccessible links. Separate mathematical proof from computational checking.

   artofproblemsolving.com/community/q1_ · khanacademy.org/search?page_search_query= ·
   overleaf.com/docs?encoded_snip= · latex.codecogs.com/png.image? · docs.google.com/forms/...viewform?usp=pp_url
   (Forms only with entry.N IDs I paste in) · plus any URL I give you or that appears in this prompt's whitelist table.

   URLs, DIKSHA dial codes, Wolfram quiz/demo slugs not in my table, or mathsolver.microsoft.com (dead site).

title: Student Doubt to Three Human Explanations
whatYouGet: A level-appropriate first explanation plus focused searches for three genuinely different human-written approaches.

title: Sequence Identity With OEIS Evidence
whatYouGet: A cautious sequence identification with computed terms, competing matches and an OEIS reading guide.
howToUse: Paste the rule or known terms, verify at least six terms, then inspect every plausible OEIS match rather than the first result.
effectiveUsage: 1. Paste all known terms and the way they were generated.
2. Check the recomputed term list against the source.
3. Open the OEIS search and inspect several candidates.
4. Accept an identity only after its recurrence or formula matches the original construction.
commonFix: If wrong, reply with: "Compute more terms, include the offset and show why each competing OEIS match does or does not fit the generating rule."

CONTEXT: A learner has encountered [SEQUENCE TERMS OR RULE] and wants to know what sequence it may be.

INPUTS — FILL EVERY PLACEHOLDER:

SOURCE-BOUND TOOL FACTS AND EXACT URL WHITELIST:

DO THIS:
1. Recompute at least six to eight consecutive terms and state the indexing offset.
2. Search exact comma-separated terms in OEIS without spaces or invented entry IDs.
3. List multiple plausible matches when the finite prefix is ambiguous.
4. Compare recurrence, formula, offset and mathematical context against the supplied construction.
5. Explain that matching a finite prefix is evidence of identity, not proof.
6. Give one next term or structural check that best separates the candidates.

WORKED LINK EXAMPLE — COPY THIS EXACT ENCODING PATTERN:
